epics.title: Retrieval Metadata Model
epics.intent: Evolve simple sidecar search fields into a richer retrieval profile that supports hybrid semantic, lexical, faceted, and role/task-based search without rendering internal terms in policy bodies.
outcomes: A proposed retrieval metadata shape that can coexist with current search fields during migration.
Clear term categories for canonical terms, aliases, legacy terms, task queries, role terms, trigger terms, artifact terms, facets, and semantic query examples.
Guidance for which retrieval terms should be curated by humans versus generated as suggestions.
dependencies: Human review workflow for accepting generated metadata
acceptance_criteria: The model distinguishes visible document text from internal retrieval signals.
The model supports SNF vocabulary variation such as EOP, emergency plan, disaster plan, command center, labor pool, and evacuation terms.
The model supports agent-friendly task queries such as what to do first, who needs to be notified, and which form is used.
The model remains sidecar-first and does not require changes to policy body content.
epics.notes: This is not SEO for public web discovery. It is structured retrieval support for BrightSource-style hybrid search and agentic RAG.

epics.title: Document Graph Expansion
epics.intent: Expand the document graph from curated pilot links into a managed network of curated edges, detected mentions, confidence-scored suggestions, evidence spans, backlinks, and promotion workflows.
outcomes: Direct title and alias mentions can become suggested graph edges with evidence spans.
Curated edges remain separate from generated suggestions until reviewed.
Backlinks and related-document views can support navigation, review, and RAG context planning.
Policies that mention tools, forms, charts, or companion policies can surface those resources quickly.
dependencies: Human review workflow for suggested edges
acceptance_criteria: Generated suggestions include source doc_id, target doc_id, relationship type candidate, confidence, and evidence span.
Duplicate curated edges and invalid doc_ids remain validation failures in the main graph workflow.
Detected mentions do not automatically become curated related_documents entries.
Graph outputs can support both forward links and backlinks.
epics.notes: Important edge types include uses_artifact, companion, prerequisite, supports, see_also, and future training-specific edges.

epics.title: Agentic RAG Affordances
epics.intent: Define tool-friendly metadata records that help an agent know what a document can answer, what it can generate, what extra context it requires, and which outputs are safe to produce.
outcomes: Documents can advertise answerable question classes and safe generation tasks.
Agents can identify required context before producing forms, summaries, notifications, or training updates.
Chunk-level retrieval IDs can support grounded retrieval, citations, and change impact analysis.
Related tools and forms can be discovered as part of the same retrieval plan.
dependencies: Artifact metadata for forms and tools
acceptance_criteria: The proposed records are machine-readable and easy for tools to consume.
The records can express can_answer, can_generate, requires_context, safe_outputs, related tools/forms, and chunk-level retrieval IDs.
The records distinguish policy explanation from client-specific generation that needs facility data.
The records are planning metadata only and do not change publishable document bodies.
epics.notes: This supports future agents that can answer, assemble, update, or route work while staying grounded in approved source documents.

epics.title: Education Metadata
epics.intent: Capture training relevance and change-impact signals so future education workflows can identify affected audiences, competencies, training triggers, quiz affordances, and suggested learning outputs.
outcomes: Policies can indicate when content has training implications.
Audience and role metadata can support assignment suggestions for staff education.
Competency domains and triggers can guide future quiz or microlearning generation.
Change-impact prompts can help agents ask whether staff re-education is needed after policy updates.
dependencies: Human review workflow for education suggestions
acceptance_criteria: The metadata can express training relevance, affected audiences, roles, competency domains, training triggers, suggested learning outputs, quiz affordances, and change-impact prompts.
The metadata can point to future training material without requiring training content to exist now.
Suggested education affordances remain reviewable before becoming curated.
The metadata supports annual review and policy-change workflows.
epics.notes: This is intended to prevent customized policy training from becoming too labor-intensive to maintain.

epics.title: Training Graph Edges
epics.intent: Reserve and define graph relationship types that connect policies, artifacts, roles, competency evidence, and future training materials.
outcomes: Training-specific edge types are named early enough to avoid later graph rework.
Policy-to-training and role-to-knowledge relationships can be represented distinctly.
Future education agents can traverse from policy changes to suggested training updates.
acceptance_criteria: Reserved edge types include requires_training, supports_training, quiz_source_for, role_must_know, annual_education_topic, and training_evidence_for.
Training edges can be suggested separately from curated operational document links.
The graph can express policy-to-policy, policy-to-artifact, policy-to-training, and role-to-document relationships.
The vocabulary remains directional and does not force current training module implementation.
epics.notes: These edges are expected to matter most once policy updates and education assignments become connected workflows.

epics.title: BrightSource v2 Directional Interfaces
epics.intent: List likely index outputs and metadata feeds BrightSource could consume without turning this planning backlog into product requirements or UI specification work.
outcomes: Future consumers can see likely interface shapes for retrieval, graph, education, export, and review metadata.
The repo can evolve indexes with BrightSource in mind while avoiding premature app commitments.
Planning remains grounded in sidecar-first metadata and generated views.
acceptance_criteria: The backlog explicitly states BrightSource v2 integration is directional only.
Candidate outputs are described as likely feeds, not final app contracts.
No UI requirements, workflow commitments, or product specs are created in this pass.
The direction supports hybrid semantic, graph, lexical, and agentic retrieval use cases.
epics.notes: This is the bridge between repo metadata architecture and future product discovery, not a substitute for that discovery.

epics.title: Human Review Workflow
epics.intent: Define how suggested retrieval terms, graph links, education affordances, and agentic RAG records are reviewed before being promoted to curated metadata.
outcomes: Generated suggestions can be inspected, accepted, rejected, or edited by a human reviewer.
Curated metadata remains explainable and traceable to evidence.
Review decisions can be stored separately before being applied to sidecars.
The workflow can reuse the existing HTML review affordance pattern where helpful.
acceptance_criteria: Suggestions are never silently promoted to curated metadata.
Reviewer decisions can capture accept, reject, edit, defer, and needs-source-review states.
Accepted decisions can later be applied safely to document.meta.json sidecars.
The workflow can identify low-confidence or high-impact suggestions for human review.
epics.notes: This keeps the system ambitious without letting generated metadata quietly become policy truth.
